title: Graceful stream retry contract and opaque id-key recommendations
creator: Aisha Thompson
description:
Problem: Cross-language SDKs currently have inconsistent retry/backoff defaults and divergent idempotency ergonomics for streaming and chunked requests. This causes confusion for customers integrating long-running streams (chat, file uploads, long generations) where partial progress, cost, and duplicate side-effects must be accounted for.

Goal: Define a single ergonomic contract and set of recommended defaults that work across Python/TS/Go:
- Default retry/backoff presets (interactive vs throughput vs bulk) with concrete numbers and rationales.
- A minimal opaque idempotency key contract for request-level deduping and a resume token pattern for partial streams.
- A retryable error taxonomy and per-language examples/code snippets demonstrating correct usage.
- Telemetry requirements and migration guidance for existing SDK consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Documented retry presets (interactive/standard/bulk) with exact parameters usable by SDK implementers
An opaque id-key contract doc that server and SDKs agree on (header name, TTL, dedupe scope, suggested generation), plus examples in Python/TS/Go
A streaming resume pattern with a resume_token response field and client behavior for resume vs full retry
A retryable error taxonomy (network, transient backend, throttling, model-timeout, non-retriable-conflict) with mapping to HTTP codes and client actions
SDK PRs (python/ts/go) that implement defaults and helper utilities (IdKey generator, RetryPolicy builder) merged behind feature flags
End-to-end tests demonstrating no duplicate side-effects for a simulated flaky server and stream resume working within grace window
implementation_plan:
1) Finalize contract doc and get sign-off from runtime and API teams. 2) Add shared constants and helpers in internal sdk-common repo: RetryPresets, IdKey utility, StreamResume helpers. 3) Implement language adapters: python context manager + helper, ts AbortSignal integration + helper, go context-aware helper. 4) Add tests: unit for backoff math, integration tests against flaky testserver that emits controlled errors and resume tokens. 5) Telemetry: emit retry_count, last_error_category, resumed:bool, id_key_used. 6) Rollout behind opt-in feature flag for 2 weeks, collect metrics, then enable by default.

Notes: prioritize ergonomics for interactive/low-latency paths; ensure bulk presets prioritize throughput and get built-in jitter to avoid thundering herd.
decisions: Use opaque id-key header name: X-Redwood-Id-Key
Id-key semantics: server dedupe window = 60s by default, configurable per-route; SDKs must surface generation helper but not enforce server TTL
Resume semantics: server returns resume_token in final stream event or as a trailing header; client can attempt resume within grace_window (default 30s) using Resume-Token header
Retry default: jittered exponential backoff with base=100ms, factor=2, max_backoff=10s for interactive; higher caps for bulk preset
Language ergonomics: Python exposes RetryPolicy object + context manager; TS exposes RetryPolicy builder + AbortSignal; Go uses RetryPolicy with context.Context cancellation and helper wrappers
tradeoffs:
- Short id-key dedupe windows reduce accidental duplicate side-effects but increase chance of not covering long client retries; we choose 60s default as conservative balance.
- Resume token approach requires server support and state; fallback is re-issuing full request which may be expensive. We accept complexity on the server side to avoid duplicate side-effects in most streaming scenarios.
- Enabling opt-in feature flag delays benefit but avoids breaking existing clients; adds short-term maintenance overhead.
- The client helper will generate opaque ids by default which is easiest for customers, but we allow passing custom keys to support enterprise audit flows.
test_plan: Unit tests for backoff math and jitter distribution across languages
Integration test harness: flaky testserver that returns controlled 500/429 and yields a resume_token on partial success; confirm client resumes correctly and server dedupes duplicates
Property tests for id-key uniqueness and header propagation
E2E test: simulate 100 concurrent interactive streams with intermittent network drops; measure resumed:true fraction and duplicate side-effect rate=0
Telemetry validation: retry_count histogram, resumed ratio, id_key_present percentage
rollout_plan:
Week 1: merge behind 'graceful-stream-retry' feature flag and release alpha SDK versions. Week 2: invite 5-10 beta customers and internal teams to opt in. Monitor telemetry (retry_count, resumed, duplicates). If no regressions after 2 weeks, flip flag for new minor release and publish migration notes. If issues, revert default and iterate on parameters.

Communication: announce on #sdk-dev, update changelogs, and include short migration guide in SDK docs.
docs_tasks: Author 'Retry & Idempotency' section in SDK reference: definitions, examples, and recommended presets
Add per-language example snippets: python context manager example, ts AbortSignal usage, go context wrapper
Write migration notes for customers currently providing custom id-keys
Design doc for server-side resume_token behavior and ledger TTLs (link below)
